snap_federal.figures_effective: SNAP federal fiscal year 2027, Oct. 1, 2026 through Sept. 30, 2027 (USDA eligibility page); Texas Works Handbook tables revision 26-4 effective Oct. 1, 2026; average benefit is the FY 2026 annual summary row (data as of September 11, 2026).

description.note: Federal 130% gross and 100% net limits, resource limits $3,000 and $4,750, net-only test for elderly or disabled households, maximum allotments $306 (1 person) and $1,023 (4 people), 30 day decision and 7 day expedited path, and the note that non-citizen and work rules changed under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025: USDA eligibility page (information for Oct. 1, 2026 through Sept. 30, 2027). Lone Star Card: Texas HHSC SNAP page. Texas 165% gross limit for categorically eligible households: Texas Works Handbook B-471 and C-121.

eligibility.income_limit_pct_fpl.evidence: gross income less than or equal to 165 percent of the Federal Poverty Income Limit
eligibility.income_limit_pct_fpl.note: Texas gross income limit for categorically eligible households (Texas Works Handbook B-471, revision 15-4); the C-121 table effective Oct. 1, 2026 has a 165% column that it calls the income limit for categorically eligible households. Federal baseline: USDA table header 'Gross monthly income (130% of poverty)' and 'Net monthly income (100% of poverty)'. Households with an elderly or disabled member only face the net test. Recorded the Texas applicable limit per Appendix A4; federal baseline is stated in the description. Also read, not matched against this snippet: the federal baseline table at https://www.fna.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility and the 165% column of table C-121 at https://fhb.hhs.texas.gov/handbooks/texas-works-handbook/c-120-supplemental-nutrition-assistance-program.

eligibility.citizenship_required.evidence: limits eligibility for SNAP benefits to U.S. citizens and certain lawfully present non-citizens
eligibility.citizenship_required.note: USDA banner on the eligibility page and on the non-citizen policy page says both are being updated for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025 changes to non-citizen eligibility. The specific non-citizen criteria listed on the eligibility page may therefore be out of date. The non-citizen page https://www.fna.usda.gov/snap/recipient/eligibility/non-citizen carries only the banner and does not repeat the snippet.

estimated_monthly_value_usd.note: National average monthly benefit per household: ANNUAL SUMMARY row for FY 2026 in the PDF of the USDA SNAP National View Summary (data as of September 11, 2026; monthly data through June 2026). Row columns: participation persons, participation households, benefit costs, average monthly benefit per person (189.15), average monthly benefit per household (348.89). The Excel version of the same table shows 348.8948, rounded to cents. FY 2025 full year was 353.42 and June 2026 was 342.35. This is a national average; USDA publishes no Texas-specific average. The PDF and Excel files are linked from https://www.fna.usda.gov/pd/supplemental-nutrition-assistance-program-snap and redirect from www.fna.usda.gov to a CDN host.

processing_time_days.evidence: whether or not you are eligible for benefits within 30 days
processing_time_days.note: USDA: state agency sends a notice within 30 days of the application in most cases; expedited path is within 7 days for households meeting extra requirements.

documents_needed.note: Texas HHSC list for SNAP plus the general items (identity, immigration status, residence). Page says you do not need to send all items and HHSC will say which are needed.

application_url.note: method: http. Texas HHSC SNAP page says 'Apply at YourTexasBenefits.com.' and links to this page.

medicaid_federal.figures_effective: Income bands are from the Medicaid.gov Texas state profile table headed 'as of December 1, 2023' (read 2026-10-13). Processing standard is 42 CFR 435.912 as shown on eCFR; immigration rule as shown on HealthCare.gov. Estimated monthly value is MACPAC Exhibit 22, FY 2023 (published February 2026).

description.note: Program definition, groups covered, immigration-status limit and lawfully-residing option: HealthCare.gov Medicaid and CHIP page. Texas pathways (Children's Medicaid, CHIP, Pregnant Women, CHIP Perinatal, Parents and Caretakers, MEPD): Texas HHSC program pages. States set income levels within federal rules, MAGI tied to FPL: Medicaid.gov Texas state profile. 45 and 90 day standards: 42 CFR 435.912.

eligibility.income_limit_pct_fpl.evidence: Income eligibility levels are tied to the federal poverty level (FPL).
eligibility.income_limit_pct_fpl.note: Highest Medicaid MAGI band in the Texas profile (Eligibility in Texas section, table dated December 1, 2023, so possibly stale at source). Bands: Medicaid ages 0-1 198%, ages 1-5 144%, ages 6-18 133%, pregnant women Medicaid 198%, parent/caretaker 12%, expansion to adults No. Separate CHIP is 201% and is not counted here because it is a different program (chip_tx). Read in the built-in browser pane 2026-10-13; the section is collapsed until clicked. The percentages are filled in by the page's scripts, so they are absent from the plain HTML snapshot and the machine evidence check can only match the sentence above; the rendered rows read 'Medicaid Ages 0-1 198%', 'Separate CHIP 201%', 'Pregnant Women Medicaid 198%' and 'Parent/Caretaker 12%'.

eligibility.citizenship_required.evidence: only people with the following immigration statuses are now eligible for full
eligibility.citizenship_required.note: HealthCare.gov lists Lawful Permanent Resident, Cuban or Haitian entrant, and COFA migrant; depending on the state, lawfully residing pregnant women and children may be eligible. Medicaid.gov Texas profile footnote says other criteria apply 'with respect to citizenship, immigration status and residency'. U.S. citizens are not named in the HealthCare.gov list but the status rule is the qualifying-status rule. The Medicaid.gov Texas profile footnote is at https://www.medicaid.gov/state-overviews/stateprofile.html?state=Texas (read, not matched against this snippet).

estimated_monthly_value_usd.note: MACPAC MACStats Exhibit 22 (Medicaid and CHIP Data Book, February 2026), FY 2023, Texas row, Total, All enrollees column = $7,958 per full-year equivalent enrollee; the Full-benefit enrollees column is $8,701 and the lower All enrollees figure is used. Medicaid benefit spending only (MACPAC analysis of T-MSIS and CMS-64 data); excludes administrative costs. Texas footnote 9 concerns the new adult group, not this column. 7958 / 12 = 663.17, rounded to 663. This is government spending averaged over all Texas enrollees, not a benefit paid to the household. FY 2023 is the most recent year in the exhibit.

estimate.represents: Government Medicaid benefit spending per full-year equivalent Texas enrollee (all groups, all enrollees), per month, not cash paid to the household.

processing_time_days.evidence: 90 days for applicants who apply for Medicaid on the basis of disability
processing_time_days.note: 42 CFR 435.912(c)(3): '(i) 90 days for applicants who apply for Medicaid on the basis of disability; and (ii) 45 days for all other applicants.' Recorded 90, the upper bound, per the data convention; the 45 day standard for all other applicants is in the description. Cited through the eCFR renderer service because the regular page returns a bot-check page to plain HTTP; the text is the same.

documents_needed.note: Texas HHSC list for Medicaid for an Adult or Pregnant Woman and Children's Medicaid (income, medical costs, citizenship) plus the general items (identity, immigration status, residence).

application_url.note: method: http. Texas HHSC 'Apply for Medicaid' links on its Medicaid program pages go to this page.

wic_federal.figures_effective: WIC income eligibility guidelines effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027; average monthly benefit is the Texas FY 2025 row (data as of September 11, 2026).

description.note: Who is eligible, nutritional risk, 185% income standard, priority system and income guideline table: USDA WIC FAQ, eligibility page and 2026-2027 income guidelines notice. Texas $2,461 and $5,088 monthly figures and application steps, how long women, infants and children stay on WIC: Texas WIC apply page. Citizenship not required: Texas HHSC WIC General Information page.

eligibility.income_limit_pct_fpl.evidence: must fall at or below 185 percent of the U.S. Poverty Income Guidelines
eligibility.income_limit_pct_fpl.note: Federal maximum; states may set lower limits but not above 185% or below 100%. Texas HHSC states 'Households with incomes at or below 185 percent of the federal poverty income level are eligible', and the Texas WIC monthly figures ($2,461 for 1, $5,088 for 4) match the federal 185% column. Gross income. Applicants and children who receive Medicaid, SNAP or TANF can meet the income test. Also read, not matched against this snippet: https://www.hhs.texas.gov/providers/wic-providers/wic-general-information (Texas 185 percent statement) and the Federal Register notice page https://www.fna.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926 (annual income eligibility guidelines).

eligibility.citizenship_required.evidence: U.S. citizenship is not a requirement for eligibility.
eligibility.citizenship_required.note: Texas HHSC WIC General Information page (provider section of hhs.texas.gov). No equivalent sentence was found on a readable USDA page (the USDA non-citizen communities page is archived).

estimated_monthly_value_usd.note: USDA WIC PROGRAM: AVERAGE MONTHLY BENEFIT PER PERSON (PDF), Texas row; columns are FY 2021 to FY 2025, so 50.49 is FY 2025 (data as of September 11, 2026). The Excel version shows 50.4878, rounded to cents. National FY 2025 average is 64.89. Per participant, not per household. The workbook says FY 2025 data are preliminary and the PDF says data are subject to revision. The files are linked from https://www.fna.usda.gov/pd/wic-program and redirect from www.fna.usda.gov to a CDN host.

processing_time_days.evidence: All other applicants shall be notified of their eligibility or ineligibility within 20 days
processing_time_days.note: 7 CFR 246.7: applicants at special nutritional risk (including eligible pregnant women) within 10 days, extendable to 15; all other applicants within 20 days of the first request for benefits. Used the 20 day upper bound. Cited through the eCFR renderer service because plain HTTP to the regular page https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/part-246/section-246.7 returns a bot-check page instead of the regulation; both show the same text.

documents_needed.note: USDA How to Apply page lists identification for each person enrolling, proof of address, and proof of SNAP/Medicaid/TANF enrollment or proof of income. Texas WIC apply page says the local office will list what is needed, typically proof of address, benefits programs, income and identification. The Texas WIC apply page https://www.texaswic.org/apply uses different wording and does not repeat the snippet.

application_url.note: method: http. Texas WIC apply page offers 'Apply Online Now' and a phone number.

liheap_federal.figures_effective: Texas CEAP eligibility at 150% of the 2026 federal poverty income guidelines, effective January 26, 2026 (TDHCA). The LIHEAP model plan PDF that TDHCA links as '2027 LIHEAP Plan' is headed Federal Fiscal Year 2026. Estimated monthly value is the ACF Texas FY2023 state profile (data as of April 30, 2024).

description.note: Purpose, no fee and no direct grants to individuals: ACF LIHEAP page. CEAP description and 254 counties: TDHCA CEAP page. 150% of 2026 guidelines, $23,940 and $49,500: TDHCA income guidelines page. TDHCA does not accept applications from individuals and providers may be at capacity: TDHCA Help for Texans. Citizenship verification, 48 hour and 18 hour crisis response: Texas LIHEAP model plan PDF.

eligibility.income_limit_pct_fpl.note: Texas CEAP threshold; the Texas LIHEAP model plan also lists 150% of USHHS poverty guidelines for heating, cooling and crisis components. Federal law lets states use up to 150% of poverty or 60% of state median income, and households receiving TANF, SSI or SNAP can also be eligible under the statute text reproduced in the plan. The 150% eligibility threshold is also in the model plan at https://www.tdhca.texas.gov/sites/default/files/community-affairs/docs/27-LIHEAP.pdf (read, not matched against this snippet).

eligibility.citizenship_required.evidence: LIHEAP recipients are U.S. citizens or qualified non-citizens who are eligible to receive LIHEAP benefits
eligibility.citizenship_required.note: From the Texas LIHEAP model plan section 17.3 (citizenship and legal residency verification). Verification is per household member and uses SAVE for non-citizens. The TDHCA SAVE FAQ PDF linked from its Household Status Verification page returned 404. The TDHCA CEAP page https://www.tdhca.texas.gov/comprehensive-energy-assistance-program-ceap was listed earlier but does not state the citizenship rule.

documents_needed.evidence: Applicants must submit current utility bill
documents_needed.note: Texas LIHEAP model plan sections 17.2 to 17.8: government-issued identification, income documentation for all adult household members (pay stubs, Social Security award letters, bank statements and similar), current utility bill and proof of residency, documentation of citizenship or immigration status. The plan's table is unclear on whether Social Security numbers are required or only requested, so they are not listed.

estimated_monthly_value_usd.evidence: Cooling Assistance served 75,317 households with reported average benefits of $1,751
estimated_monthly_value_usd.note: ACF LIHEAP Texas FY2023 State Profile (data current as of April 30, 2024): Heating Assistance served 47,945 households with reported average benefits of $2,750 (regular LIHEAP funds); Cooling Assistance served 75,317 households with average benefits of $1,751 (regular funds). Year-round crisis average ($3,502) is excluded because it is not a regular benefit. No combined average is published, so the lower figure is used (tie-break). min(2750, 1751) / 12 = 145.9, rounded to 146. Possibly stale at source: FY2024 and FY2025 profile files were not found at the same address; the ACF Texas page (https://liheapch.acf.gov/profiles/Texas.htm, last updated 04/20/2026) lists households served in FY 2024 but no average.

estimate.represents: Average yearly LIHEAP household benefit in Texas (fiscal year 2023, lower of cooling and heating), spread evenly over 12 months; actual help is seasonal or one-time, not a monthly payment.

processing_time_days.note: Null: the Texas LIHEAP plan re-read 2026-10-13 states response times only for crisis cases (48 hours, 18 hours if life threatening), which are not the regular standard. The plan's other time limits (written denial notice within 10 calendar days of a determination, appeal windows) are not a processing standard for applications. TDHCA community affairs pages checked in Phase 1 state none.

medicare_extra_help_federal.figures_effective: 2026 income and resource limits (Medicare.gov, 'Income and resource limits in 2026'); Medicare.gov also shows 2027 cost-sharing for the upcoming year; SSA POMS HI 03001.020 effective 02/11/2026. Estimated monthly value is from SSA publication EN-05-10508, August 2026.

description.note: What Extra Help does, automatic enrollment, 2026 dollar limits, territories exclusion: Medicare.gov help with drug costs. Part A or B, 50 states or DC, income under 150% of FPL: SSA POMS HI 03001.020. How to apply: SSA Extra Help page. Citizenship or status rule for joining a drug plan: Medicare.gov joining a plan page.

eligibility.income_limit_pct_fpl.evidence: must be less than 150% of the FPL (based on size of the household)
eligibility.income_limit_pct_fpl.note: SSA Program Operations Manual: income after exclusions must be less than 150% of the FPL. Medicare.gov shows the 2026 dollar equivalents ($23,940 individual, $32,460 couple) but states them in dollars only, so the percent comes from POMS. Resource limits are separate and apply too. The Medicare.gov dollar limits are at https://www.medicare.gov/basics/costs/help/drug-costs (read, not matched against this snippet).

eligibility.citizenship_required.evidence: Be a U.S. citizen or U.S. national, a lawful permanent resident (green card holder),
eligibility.citizenship_required.note: Indirect: Medicare.gov states this as a condition for joining a Medicare health or drug plan, and POMS HI 03001.020 requires that the Extra Help applicant enroll with a Part D plan or MA-PD. No Extra Help page states the citizenship rule in so many words. The POMS page https://secure.ssa.gov/poms.nsf/lnx/0603001020 was read for the enrollment point but does not repeat the snippet.

estimated_monthly_value_usd.note: SSA publication EN-05-10508, 'Understanding the Extra Help with Your Medicare Prescription Drug Plan', August 2026; read in the built-in browser from ssa.gov (text extracted from the PDF). SSA states it per beneficiary per year. 5700 / 12 = 475.

estimate.represents: SSA's stated average yearly worth of Extra Help per beneficiary, spread evenly over 12 months; individual amounts depend on plan and drug use.

inputs.evidence: Extra Help is estimated to be worth about $5,700 per year.

processing_time_days.note: Null: re-read 2026-10-13. The SSA Extra Help application page, SSA publication EN-05-10508 (August 2026), Medicare.gov drug-costs page and the Medicare.gov Extra Help fact sheet state no time to decide an application. Only a 10 day reply window after a pre-decisional notice, a 30 day review-form window and a 60 day appeal window appear, and those are not processing standards.

ssdi_federal.figures_effective: 2026 SGA and work-credit figures (SSA); average disabled-worker benefit for August 2026 (Monthly Statistical Snapshot released September 2026); processing FAQ dated March 5, 2024.

description.note: Eligibility, 5 of 10 years work history and under-24 exception, 2026 SGA amounts: SSA Who can get Disability page. Five-month waiting period and conversion at full retirement age: SSA How Does Someone Become Eligible page. Medicare after 2 years: SSA What you could get page. Average benefit: Monthly Statistical Snapshot, August 2026. 6 to 8 months: SSA FAQ KA-01801. Lawful presence: SSA FAQ KA-02447.

eligibility.citizenship_required.evidence: Lawfully present noncitizens of the United States who meet all eligibility requirements can qualify
eligibility.citizenship_required.note: SSA FAQ (dated December 30, 2022) says lawfully present noncitizens who meet all requirements can qualify. U.S. citizens can qualify as well, so citizenship itself is not required, but undocumented non-citizens are not covered; recorded true as 'citizen or qualifying status' per Appendix A4. Possibly stale at source (2022).

eligibility.requires_disability.evidence: must have a disability that affects your ability to work for a year or more
eligibility.requires_disability.note: Every path to SSDI requires a qualifying disability or blindness (SSA Who can get Disability). The page https://www.ssa.gov/benefits/disability/qualify.html says the same in other words (a medical condition that meets Social Security's strict definition of disability) and does not repeat the snippet.

eligibility.income_limit_pct_fpl.note: Null: SSDI has no percent-of-poverty income test. Eligibility rests on a disability and work credits; earnings above the substantial gainful activity amount ($1,690 a month in 2026, $2,830 if blind) can block eligibility, but that is a dollar earnings test on work, not an FPL limit.

estimated_monthly_value_usd.note: Monthly Statistical Snapshot, August 2026, Table 2, Disability Insurance, Disabled workers, Average monthly benefit (dollars) 1,635.90. National average.

processing_time_days.evidence: it generally takes 6 to 8 months for an initial decision
processing_time_days.note: Upper bound 8 months converted at 30 days per month = 240 days. FAQ is dated March 5, 2024; SSA's performance pages say the average initial decision time has been falling (values are in charts, not text). Possibly stale at source.

estimate.represents: SSA's stated upper bound of 8 months for an initial decision, converted to days at 30 days per month.
